title: White cabaret pianists in New Orleans, c.1912-14
summary: He recalls Erwin LeClaire, Leonard Beisdorfer and Joe Virgis playing cabarets; he did not hear Tony Jackson.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, in those days, uh, I think that the boys that we played with will remember Erwin LeClaire. I don't think that Erwin ever really followed his music, as well as, uh, Leonard Beisdorfer and, uh, Joe Virgis. Uh, Joe Virgis had composed some tunes in his day, and he was quite a well-known pianist, as well as Beisdorfer. They played mostly, they played mostly the cabarets.
There was a Beisdorfer who, uh, played, uh, trumpets. Was he related?
It may have been. I didn't know him. But I knew Leonard Beisdorfer was a pianist, and he was a good one.
Are these, uh, white or colored boys?
No. No. They played cabarets. Mostly.
Um, uh, Tony Jackson may have been a prominent, uh, party pianist then. Have you heard him there? No. Or Kelly Rowell?
Uh, this, uh, period you're talking about was around 1912, 14?
